version: "3.9"
services: postgres: image: postgres:16 container_name: flashcard-postgres-qa environment: POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB} POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER} POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD} ports: - "${DB_PORT:-5433}:5432" volumes: - postgres_qa_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data healthcheck: test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER} -d ${POSTGRES_DB}"] interval: 5s timeout: 5s retries: 10
api: build: context: . dockerfile: Dockerfile container_name: flashcard-api-qa environment: ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT: QA ConnectionStrings__Default: ${DB_CONNECTION_STRING} depends_on: postgres: condition: service_healthy ports: - "${API_PORT:-8081}:8080"
volumes: postgres_qa_data:

option.name: updatedContent
option.value:
# Kubernetes configuration layout
This project follows a single Kubernetes config pattern with environment-specific files:
- `k8s/dev/configmap-dev.yaml` - `k8s/dev/secret-dev.yaml` - `k8s/qa/configmap-qa.yaml` - `k8s/qa/secret-qa.yaml` - `k8s/prod/configmap-prod.yaml` - `k8s/prod/secret-prod.yaml`
The naming convention clearly identifies the environment and the resource type, which keeps config values easier to reason about and avoids mixing dev/qa/prod settings together.
